text.p: The Philippine central bank has lowered its monetary supply ceilings until the end of the year in a bid to defend the peso from any speculative attack, central bank documents showed.

The documents made available to reporters on Sunday showed M3 or broad money ceiling for this year will be cut by 29.9 billion pesos ($1 billion) to 1,026.8 billion pesos ($35.5 billion) from the original level of 1,056.7 billion.
The changes mean that M3, the broadest measure of liquidity, is to be allowed to grow by only 16.5 percent in 1997 instead of 19.9 percent, the papers showed.
At the end of 1996, M3 stood at 881.4 billion pesos, which was up 15 percent from the previous year.
Since the local currency was effectively devalued three weeks ago, the central bank has taken several measures to reduce the supply of pesos.
It raised overnight lending rates to a 2-1/2 year high of 32 percent. It later brought them down again but the rate still remains at a relative high of 22 percent.
The bank also doubled the liquidity reserve requirement for banks to four percent. ($ = 28.9 Philippine Pesos)
